title: Lumberjack's CUSTOM Junkyard LS is DONE! First Fire Up! (1,500hp?)
coverage: full transcript read (0:00-56:00); 0:00-3:45 music/intro montage, 3:45-9:39 unrelated swan segment

context.edition: CRC 2 (Sick Summer leg) per caller labelling - Lumberjack engine build
context.timing_note: Said to be on the key for Sick Summer and filmed at end of 'Month of Freedom'; but captions also say BTR gaskets were obtained 'while we were out on six summer' - exact order vs the event is unclear (low confidence)

cars.build_snapshot: 'CNS (Cleetus and Squirrel) serial #1' engine + 'CNS serial #1' transmission

engine.block: aluminum LS block (their 'old aluminum girl'), cylinders crosshatch-honed at Fast Forward; uses small-bore (5.3-bore) gaskets
engine.heads: existing heads reused ('flattest heads on the planet'), old valve springs reused
engine.cam: old Lumberjack cam reused (an NA-type cam; replacement on order)
engine.rotating_assembly: Texas Speed balanced assembly: brand-new stock GM LS crank (balanced), forged H-beam rods, pistons with coated skirts; spiral-lock wrist-pin retainers; 0.927 in wrist pins
engine.head_gasket: Brian Tooley Racing MLS, LS9-style multi-layer in small 5.3 bore size
engine.head_studs: BTR head studs (also bought for backup motor)

build_specs.fact: Wrist pin diameter measured 0.927 in; rod pin-bore honed to ~0.0009-0.0011 in clearance
Top ring end-gap target ~0.026 in (file-fit rings)
Main bearing clearance ~0.0021 in (ideal 0.0023-0.0024; aluminum block grows) - warm up before hard launches
Main caps: 15 ft-lb + 80 deg inner, 15 ft-lb + 51 deg outer
Rod bearing clearances all in spec, tightest at edge
Scratch found and polished out of main journals
Pistons mistakenly installed with wrong orientation during assembly and corrected

power_targets.fact: Hoped 1,100-1,200 hp; likely first failure point is the head gasket
Joe: ~40 psi and 20 deg timing about the limit for these parts; team suggests ~29 psi at 11 deg, Joe would run 15-16 deg
Pistons said to be good for ~1,500 (hp implied)

power_adder.notes: turbo found full of rainwater before install

transmission.notes: 'CNS serial #1' transmission built with Cameron Powers; torque converter installed

fuel.notes: fuel pump stuck from sitting on E85; freed by striking it; gas cap had been loose

cars.ecu_notes: no-start fixed by TPS auto-calibration; 12 psi oil pressure while cranking; 13.8 V running

parts.part: Texas Speed balanced rotating assembly (pistons/rods charged to budget; stock crank)
BTR small-bore LS9-style MLS head gaskets

result.fact: Engine fired after TPS calibration; idled smooth and quiet

previous_failure_ref.fact: Previous crank was destroyed by bent rods

cars.confidence: medium-high for build specs; title's 1,500 hp not stated in video
